# HEM v0.6.2b18 — One PID calibration panel per operating mode

## Device settings

- When a verified mode-scoped PID setting exists for the same physical controller and stable HA registry key, remove the redundant original device-wide editor from the **device settings dialog**. No native entity is deleted and no saved value is migrated or changed. The old control remains visible if there is no scoped equivalent, if the scoped entity is offline while the old one is usable, or while a legacy edit is in flight or failed.
- Keep each mode's settings separate (drying, heating, cooling). A user-renamed entity ID, configuration entry ownership and mode provenance are respected; other devices never participate in deduplication.
- The PID calibration **Approve** and **Reject** proposal buttons are adjacent, with compact readable localized action names, independent status/help, and separate authorized HA `button.press` targets. Neither action is auto-pressed, enabled or combined.
- Distinguish the model-based PID calibration action from fan-capacity calibration; they previously had the same generic label. Preserve custom entity names.
- Place a manual humidity target in the control/targets category, not the PID calibration category.

## Verification and safety

- Dedicated Chromium regression across EN/EL/DE and 760/390/320px checks exact-identity deduplication, scoped choices, legacy fallback, unsaved-draft retention, distinct fan calibration, paired action placement, and precise service targets.
- Full repository CI must pass before publishing. This changes only frontend device settings presentation and test/release metadata. No physical device control policy, PID gains, storage, alarm, registry or Home Assistant runtime is modified. Update through HACS when published and reload the dashboard after restarting Home Assistant if needed.
